coldReader.confusing: teleoperation is not defined; Qwen model is not explained; 'By default' leaves the alternative open; the last line is vague.
coldReader.how_sure: Established: the 91% over 360 real trials in six new places, the 70% when chained, a person writes each new task's prompt, no comparison with other systems. Hedge: 'If this holds up'.
coldReader.the_point: Apple trained a humanoid robot on computer-generated rooms and it succeeded 91% of the time in real places it had never seen, planned on a Mac mini; chained tasks drop to 70% and a person still writes the prompts.
coldReader.unknown: Comparison with other systems; whether it works beyond the six places; what tasks the 91% covers.
coldReader.what_happened: Apple researchers put a Mac mini (M4 Pro, 64 GB) on a humanoid robot, and in 360 real trials across six unmapped places it succeeded 91% of the time. It was trained on about 300 hours of generated movement data in 1,000 computer-made rooms instead of real homes, and a Qwen model on the Mac mini plans each step with no internet.
coldReader.who_is_affected: Robot researchers and companies, who could stop depending on people's hours to collect training data.
